ImageDescription.value: This photograph was taken by me at at Lakshminarayana temple in Hosaholalu, Mandya district, Karnataka state, India. The temple was built in 1250 A.D. during the reign of Hoysala Empire King Vira Someshwara. It is considered one of the ornate examples of Hoysala architecture. The shrine and the tower over it follow a stellate design style characteristic of the Hoysala architecture.

Categories.value: CC-Zero|Self-published work|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Vaitarani Kund and Temples, Gopeshwar

ImageDescription.value:
The Vaitarani kund and group of temples is a pre-12th century Hindu pilgrim site in Gopeshwar Uttarakhand. It is located 1008 feet northwest of Gopinath temple along the hill side, and was likely built by the Katyuri dynasty.
The Vaitarani monuments are notable for their Vallabhi architecture with geometric ratios that are similar to those found near the coast of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, while being relatively uncommon in the Himalayan region. The site also has some temples that are in the Himalayan style of Nagara square plan temples.

UsageTerms.value: Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication
